text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Hungary and Austria are both prepared to consent to a possible request from NATO to keep their forces in Bosnia longer than the planned December deadline, Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti and his Austrian counterpart, Werner Fasslabend, agreed yesterday during talks in Vienna.
- The British financial monthly Euromoney has chosen Hungarian central bank president Gyorgy Suranyi the best central bank governor in Eastern Europe in 1996.
- The cabinet will discuss spending levels when it meets to consider next year's budget in second reading today.
- The government yesterday approved the transfer of HUF 6.7 billion to boost public sector wages.
- On the Media Boat at the usual breakfast attended by former finance ministers differing opinions were heard on present day economic policy.
- The customs surcharge introduced last year will be reduced by a percentage point on October 1.
- The stock exchange authority and the editorial staff of the weekly Bank&Tozsde have published the Book of Hungarian Shares '96 and is available both in Hungarian and English.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The final draft of the advertising law has been completed and can now be submitted to Parliament.
- The Defence Ministry does not support a proposal to ban land mines because this would endanger the country's defensive capability.
NEPSZABADSAG

- As Hungary is not among the nuclear threshold states, it has a vested interest in limiting the proliferation of nuclear weapons and tests, Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said in New York where he signed the nuclear non-proliferation treaty.
- The Defence Ministry announced Wednesday that Hungarian troops will participate in 18 exercises abroad next year within the scope of Partnership for Peace.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Finance Ministry's most important task next year will be to harmonise economic growth with the need for equilibrium, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said.
- Postabank has commissioned consultants Arthur Andersen to examine the books of Mezobank, in which the former firm plans to acquire a majority stake.
- A group of insurance companies led by Hungaria and will probably consist of 11 Hungarian and foreign companies covering the risks of the Paks power plant could be formed within three months.
- The German car manufacturer Audi AG will boost its purchases from Hungarian suppliers by over 200 per cent by the end of 1997, leaders of the Volkswagen concern announced.
- The general meeting of the gas firm Tigaz approved the board's report on the company's results in the first half of 1996.
- Two political parties pressed their opposition to a proposal by Coca-Cola Magyarorszag to "decorate" the Chain Bridge.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. plans to discuss a new privatisation strategy for Corvinbank soon and hopes to conclude the sale this year.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
